question: Can a persistent arrival-ordered neural speaker cache improve anonymous multi-voice tracking over independent clustering windows?
development_candidates: v3-streaming geometry with upstream segmentation defaults
v3-offline streaming geometry with upstream segmentation defaults
promotion_rule: Select on development only; require lower DER and no increase in speaker-count error, then freeze before integration. Require lower mean integration DER, no individual increase above 0.02 absolute, and silence abstention. Measure computational latency separately from input buffering.
scope: Existing AMI integration clips are previously observed. Both pretrained systems have used AMI; these checks do not establish independent generalization. Native CPU execution and streaming state are part of the experiment.
height_constraint: Preserve the restored height coefficients until a separately evaluated replacement improves individual error without further compressing prediction range. Never tune using the user's two heights.

postprocessing_development_grid.selection: Lowest development DER subject to no increase in speaker-count error; frozen before integration.

fusion_extension.hypothesis: Neural activity has stable identities but misses quiet speech; clustered acoustic activity can supply missing spans while neural anchors merge fragmented cluster labels.
fusion_extension.mapping: Map each acoustic cluster to the neural channel with greatest shared activity; many clusters may share one channel. Abstain when the best anchor is shorter than 100 ms.
fusion_extension.assignment: Within acoustic speech activity, prefer all currently active neural channels; otherwise use anchored acoustic labels.
fusion_extension.selection: Compare plain neural and fused outputs on development only, using the same frozen postprocessing grid. Select before running integration.

live_execution.acoustic_refinement: Background task, keeping neural activity updates independent of acoustic computation.
live_execution.verification: replay_streaming.py --realtime, 320 ms chunks; compare final source-clock timeline with the original rolling context control.
live_execution.timing_scope: Request processing and algorithmic input buffering are measured separately; end-of-stream refinement may take longer than a regular push.
